title: Localize TransactionalEmail subject/body strings before wiring a real email provider
rule: AX-2 — no hardcoded user-facing strings; EN/HE ARB parity

evidence.quote: /// Subject line (in English; localisation deferred to the email template).
'$parentName invited you to tutor $childName on Learning Tracker';

why: All five email subject/body getters are hardcoded English with no AppLocalizations/ARB involvement, in a bilingual EN/HE app whose 1421-key ARB parity check would not catch this since these are plain Dart string literals, not l10n keys. Impact is currently nil — the only bound implementation is LoggingTransactionalEmailService, so no real recipient has ever seen this text — but the moment a real provider (SendGrid/Firebase Extension) is wired per the file's own WAKE-UP banner, Hebrew-speaking tutors/parents will receive tutor-invite/accept/decline/revoke/resign notifications only in English.
recommendation: Route subject/body through locale-aware templates (e.g. Flutter's generated lookupAppLocalizations(locale) keyed off the recipient's stored locale, not the sender's device) before cutting over to a real provider; gate the provider cutover on this in the same Linear item that tracks provisioning.
acceptance_criteria: A Linear DNI-#### ticket exists gating real-email-provider cutover on localized templates
Once implemented, HE-locale recipients receive Hebrew subject/body; EN/HE parity is checkable the same way ARB keys are
